title: Trees & BST Journey
description: DFS orders, subtree summaries, BFS views, reconstruction, serialization, and BST operations.

journey.outcome: Choose what flows down a tree and what each subtree returns, then exploit BST ordering only when it is guaranteed.

connections.binary-tree-preorder-traversal: Visit a node before its children to make the traversal order explicit. An iterative stack must push the right child first if the left child should be visited next.
connections.binary-tree-inorder-traversal: Move the visit between the recursive calls. The same recursion skeleton changes meaning, and in a BST this order exposes values in sorted sequence.
connections.binary-tree-postorder-traversal: Delay the visit until both children finish. This order is the foundation for computing a parent's answer from completed subtree summaries.
connections.maximum-depth-of-binary-tree: Replace postorder output with one returned value: subtree depth. Define the empty subtree's value so a leaf follows the same recurrence as every other node.
connections.invert-binary-tree: Change the tree structure while preserving the recursive contract for both children. Every node swaps its own left and right subtrees exactly once.
connections.same-tree: Traverse two trees together, comparing both structure and values. Null-versus-node mismatches are just as important as unequal values.
connections.symmetric-tree: Reuse paired traversal but compare opposite children. Structural symmetry is a mirror relationship, not equality of two ordinary inorder sequences.
connections.diameter-of-binary-tree: Return height upward but also evaluate a path joining both child branches. The best complete path and the value useful to a parent are different quantities.
connections.balanced-binary-tree: Reuse subtree heights with an early failure signal. Recomputing each height from scratch at every node would repeat work and can become quadratic.
connections.path-sum: Send a remaining target downward instead of returning only heights. A root-to-leaf condition must be checked at a leaf, not at an arbitrary prefix with the right sum.
connections.binary-tree-maximum-path-sum: Generalize diameter from edge counts to weighted sums. Return one extendable branch to the parent while considering two branches only for the completed answer at the current node.
connections.subtree-of-another-tree: Reuse Same Tree at candidate roots. Separate finding a candidate location from proving that the entire structure rooted there matches.
connections.binary-tree-level-order-traversal: Change the traversal frontier from a call stack to a queue. Snapshot each layer's size before enqueueing its children so levels remain distinct.
connections.binary-tree-right-side-view: Reuse level grouping and retain the final visible node from each level. Consistent left-to-right insertion makes the last value the right-side answer.
connections.construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-: Combine the meanings of two DFS orders. Preorder identifies the root, and its inorder position separates the left and right subtrees; avoid repeatedly copying subarrays.
connections.serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree: Preserve enough information to reconstruct shape as well as values. Null markers or equivalent structure metadata distinguish trees that share the same value-only traversal.
connections.flatten-binary-tree-to-linked-list: Use preorder as the required output order while rewiring pointers. Preserve the original right subtree before attaching the flattened left subtree so no nodes become unreachable.
connections.lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree: Combine search results from two children. If both sides report a target, the current node joins the two paths; this does not require the values to be ordered.
connections.validate-binary-search-tree: Introduce the stronger BST invariant. Each node must satisfy bounds inherited from all ancestors, not only a comparison with its immediate parent.
connections.insert-into-a-binary-search-tree: Use BST comparisons to choose one child at each step. Preserve all untouched subtrees and attach the new value only when the selected search path reaches an empty child.
connections.delete-node-in-a-bst: Extend insertion's structural discipline to removal. Leaf, one-child, and two-child cases differ; the inorder successor can replace a two-child node while preserving ordering.
connections.kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst: Reuse inorder traversal as a sorted stream. Stop after the kth visit rather than sorting the whole tree or assuming subtree sizes are already available.
connections.binary-search-tree-iterator: Turn inorder traversal into a resumable interface. Retain the path to the next value in a stack instead of materializing every tree value at initialization.
connections.lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc: Revisit LCA with the extra ordering guarantee. Both targets on one side choose one child; a split across the current value identifies the ancestor immediately.
